name: Scotty Pippen Jr.
headline: Pippen Jr. is a steady energy guard on an unbeaten Grizzlies team, but the turnovers and missing threes are holding him back.
good: Memphis is 3-0 and he has played every game, averaging 7.7 points, 3.3 rebounds and 3.3 assists in 18.0 minutes.
He fills the stat sheet beyond scoring, with 1.3 steals plus blocks per game and 1.7 offensive rebounds a night.
Efficiency is fine overall: 44.4% from the field, 75% at the line and a 53.4% true shooting mark, with a 22.7% usage rate.
He had 6 rebounds (3 offensive) against Golden State and 5 assists with 5 made free throws against Utah.
bad: He averages 3.0 turnovers, including 5 in the 111-108 win over Golden State, where he was also minus 6.
He is only 16.7% from three this season (1 for 6), which hurts spacing next to other non-shooters.
His plus/minus is minus 3 total, and the model grade is a C (45) with only 3 games of data.
fans: There is little fan chatter about Pippen specifically so far. Most of the buzz is about Ty Jerome, who scored 45 against Utah and 31 against Sacramento, and rookie Cameron Boozer, who had 25 and 13 in the Golden State comeback. Preseason analysis questioned Memphis point guard depth and three-point spacing, and one preseason projection flagged Pippen's 31.3% three-point shooting last season as a concern.
outlook: Expect Pippen to keep a reserve role of around 17 to 20 minutes, with his value tied to cutting turnovers and hitting a few threes. Memphis visits Utah on Monday night (10/27, 1:00 UTC) at the Delta Center, where the Jazz are a 1.5-point favorite.
